newsitem.title: USA: Republicans stage budget victory celebration.
newsitem.headline: Republicans stage budget victory celebration.

text.p: The scene was more like that of an election victory celebration than an announcement of agreement on the first step of a long, hard road to balance the federal budget.

Minutes after President Clinton annnounced the budget accord Friday in Baltimore, beaming Republican leaders led by Senate Leader Trent Lott and House Speaker Newt Gingrich gave victory signs and hailed it in a ceremony that seemed designed to ensure that it made the history books.

They chose as their setting the magnificent domed rotunda of the U.S. Capitol, making speeches in front of an enormous painting of the signing of the Declaration of Independence and flanked by statues of George Washington and Alexander Hamilton, the first treasury secretary.
"America wins" said a blue and white sign on the front of the podium.
Gingrich called it an emotional moment, House Budget Chairman John Kasich said Gingrich was like a brother and his Senate counterpart Pete Domecici said Kasich was like a brother.
Domenici said the budget agreement was the latest of many great events that had occurred in the rotunda that had protected the American dream.

"This is another occasion when this room is being used so that the American people can realise their dreams, and their dreams as I see them are, that they be able to keep more of their hard-earned money, and we're going to see to that ..."

Hundreds of tourists were on hand, frequently erupting into applause. They included grinning 13-year-old Jose Made of intermediate school 125 in New York's borough of The Bronx, who was lifted up by Republican Sen. Connie Mack of Florida and Representative John Boehner of Ohio, and was called "my buddy Jose" by Kasich.
For Gingrich, poor public popularity ratings must have seemed a bad dream when he was mobbed by crowds eager to touch his outstretched hands after the speeches ended.
